title: Air Pollution and the Atmospheric Pollution Cycle
subtitle: Toxic Feedback Loops, Short-Lived Climate Pollutants, and the Compounding Health and Systemic Burdens in the Polycrisis Apocalypse
series: H Heuristics · Global Strategic Monograph Series · Polycrisis Series
description: H Heuristics monograph on air pollution as a polycrisis force multiplier: toxic feedback loops, short-lived climate pollutants, and a 2040 clean-air roadmap.
abstract: This 40-page strategic monograph reframes air pollution as the central transmission hub of the global polycrisis rather than a localized health externality. It traces the atmospheric pollution cycle across two destructive channels: direct biological toxicity from fine particulates and geophysical feedback from short-lived climate pollutants such as black carbon, methane, and tropospheric ozone. Across fourteen chapters, the analysis moves from PM2.5 physics and pulmonary pathology to household biomass combustion, wildfire megablazes, industrial point sources, transport non-exhaust emissions, crop toxicity, transboundary airsheds, and the macroeconomic toll on labor and human capital. The report closes with a phased 2026–2040 roadmap that prices the clean-air transition at $1.96 trillion and projects 38.2 million avoided mortalities.

bindingTerm: Read every air quality problem as a two-channel system: first ask what it does to human biology, then ask what it does to the climate, and only then price the intervention. Clean air is the highest-return investment in the polycrisis because it pays out simultaneously in lives, labor, and atmospheric stability.
